name: NY-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Lasher's large fundraising and outside spending edge
model.rationale: This Manhattan-based seat is overwhelmingly Democratic, and Micah Lasher has raised over $3.3 million with more than $10 million in outside support against a Republican who has raised about $155,000. Markets price the race near certain for Democrats, so the forecast stays close to the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A sharp national Republican wave or unexpectedly low Democratic turnout in a low-profile open seat could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jerry Nadler (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jerry Nadler's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Manhattan seat open, but the district's D+33 partisan lean makes it very difficult terrain for Republicans. Democrat Micah Lasher has built a commanding financial position, raising over $3.3 million and benefiting from more than $10 million in outside support, while Republican Caroline Shinkle has raised about $155,000 with no reported outside spending. Two independent candidates trail far behind in both money and visibility.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-thirty-point range.
